open_items.question: What are the exact unprinted segment bounds? Raster extrapolation supports only approximate bounds.

resolution.description: Adopt explicit endpoints [0,16]/[35,84]; these do not assert recovered original endpoints. All actual raw/SEM endpoints are checked against the adopted segments.

open_items.question: What are the source-reported P values or classes for the displayed comparisons?

resolution.description: Six supplied author P entries preserve the exact reported values/bound; star classes use caption thresholds, no statistical test recalculated.

open_items.question: Does each dot correspond to one biological mouse observation rather than a technical measurement?

resolution.description: Caption specifies n = 5 mice per genotype for this source panel; table contributes exactly five observations per gene/group. Biological mouse unit is caption-supported, cross-gene identities remain unknown.

open_items.question: Are observation identities shared across genes? Horizontal offsets cannot establish pairing.

resolution.description: No cross-gene matching, within-subject trajectory or paired test is drawn; source cell/local identity is not a shared mouse identity.

open_items.question: What normalization and calibrator produced relative-expression values?

resolution.description: Retain supplied relative-expression values verbatim and report upstream normalization unknown; no upstream recalculation or calibrator inference.

open_items.question: What final manuscript dimensions should be adopted?

resolution.description: Explicit standalone canvas 92 × 66 mm is adopted for this case; source physical dimensions are not asserted.

open_items.question: What exact font and final point sizes should be adopted?

resolution.description: Explicit Arial 8 pt for all visible roles; portable --font override must record its own adopted spec. Source font/pt remains unrecovered.

open_items.question: Were author P values adjusted for multiple comparisons?

resolution.description: Only supplied author P values/classes are retained and attributed, without recomputation or assertions about multiplicity handling.
